title: pullAndRefresh remains non-nonReentrant, exposing cross-frame budget double-counting via a malicious/upgraded dispatcher

classification.assetImpact: Conditional on a malicious or adversarially upgraded dispatcher: rewardBudget can be double-credited via reentry, inflating emission rate or over-reporting budget.
attackPath: 1. Dispatcher becomes malicious (upgrade or initial deployment).
3. Outer _syncBudget triggers dispatcherHook.pull() which reenters pullAndRefresh before returning.
4. Nested frame credits inflow to rewardBudget; outer frame computes inflow via balance delta that includes the nested credit - double-counting.
classification.likelihood: very low - requires dispatcher to be compromised or maliciously upgraded. Dispatcher is a trusted sibling component per spec.
classification.assumptions: Trust boundary of the dispatcher is broken.
classification.externalRequirements: Adversarial dispatcher (either initial malicious deployment or compromised upgrade).

justification: Low/QA (defence-in-depth). The dispatcher is an explicitly trusted component in the project spec. The attack vector requires the dispatcher itself to be malicious or to be upgraded to a malicious implementation - a scenario that C4 typically treats as out of scope unless the privileged party is explicitly in-scope to act adversarially. Kept as Low because missing nonReentrant on a permissionless external function is a concrete defensive-coding omission with a one-line fix. Does not meet Medium bar (no protocol-function impact under the normal trust model).
